title: Go quickly (Matthew 28:1–10)
hook: the sealed stone, an angel sitting on it, and two women running with fear and great joy
tomorrow: the guards saw everything. what will they be paid to say?

segments.voice: That was a dark week in Matthew: is it I, one hour, bitter tears, a warning washed away, a shaking earth, and a sealed stone. Yesterday's line: make it as sure as you can. They did.
screen: `MAKE IT AS SURE AS YOU CAN.` → `A WEEK IN THE DARK.`

segments.voice: A message that starts with: you're not going to believe this, and then a photo you have to see for yourself. "In the end of the sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week," Mary Magdalene and the other Mary come back to see the sepulchre. The ground moves. "And, behold, there was a great earthquake: for the angel of the Lord descended from heaven, and came and rolled back the stone from the door, and sat upon it." The stone they sealed and guarded, and someone sitting on it.
screen: `YOU'RE NOT GOING TO BELIEVE THIS.` → `A GREAT EARTHQUAKE.` → `HE SAT UPON THE STONE.`

segments.voice: "His countenance was like lightning, and his raiment white as snow." The guards, set there to make it sure, "did shake, and became as dead men." Some readers notice the turn: the watchmen look dead, and the dead man is gone. The angel speaks to the women: "Fear not ye: for I know that ye seek Jesus, which was crucified. He is not here: for he is risen, as he said." Then: "go quickly, and tell his disciples that he is risen from the dead." And they run. "And they departed quickly from the sepulchre with fear and great joy; and did run to bring his disciples word." Both at once, in the same running feet; Matthew doesn't make them choose. On the road, Jesus meets them: "All hail." They hold him by the feet and worship him. And he says: "Be not afraid: go tell my brethren that they go into Galilee, and there shall they see me." Brethren. After the sleeping, the running away and the denials, he calls them his brothers. And the ones sent running with that word are the women who stayed at the cross and sat across from the tomb, the ones who never left.
screen: `THE WATCHMEN AS DEAD MEN.` · `HE IS NOT HERE: HE IS RISEN.` · `GO QUICKLY, AND TELL.` · `GO TELL MY BRETHREN.` · then, large: `FEAR AND GREAT JOY.`

segments.voice: Before the sit, stand up and walk for about a minute, a little faster than usual, as if you were carrying news someone is waiting for. Let your heart rate rise a little. Then sit, and as your breath settles, notice whether fear and joy can sit in the same chest at once. You don't have to choose between them.
Go quickly. The angel's words to the women at the empty tomb: go, and tell his disciples he is risen, as he said.
Pocket this one: fear and great joy, carried at a run by the women who stayed. Two weeks, done.

howItsDone: Christians celebrate the resurrection at Easter, and some churches read Matthew 28 at an Easter Vigil or a sunrise service.

what it means: the first witnesses run with fear and great joy at once, sent to tell men who had fled.
what a scholar hears: χαρᾶς μεγάλης, great joy, beside φόβου, fear (28:8); the guards 'as dead men' (28:4) against the risen one; and 'my brethren' (28:10) for the disciples.
